chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Fasting becomes difficult for me in the heat, and I find a headache. He said: Do as I do. When I travel, I give charity every day with a Mudd of food, which is what I feed my family with.

key_terms.مُدٍّ: A Mudd, a traditional unit of volume for dry food (approx. 750g)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for missing fasts due to heat exhaustion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a practical alternative to fasting for those suffering from severe heat-induced headaches, prescribing the payment of *Fidya* (compensation) through daily charity. By instructing the companion to give one *Mudd* of food to his family, he links the act of expiation directly to the provision of sustenance, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on easing religious obligations (*Taysir*) when genuine hardship (*Haraj*) is present. This ruling underscores the balance between spiritual discipline and physical well-being, a key theme in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
